title: Week 6 Warm-Ups
intro: Three short review questions each day: two free-response and one multiple-choice. Every question comes from a section completed before the section scheduled for that day.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A crate rests on a level floor while a person pushes horizontally to the right. The crate does not move. Draw a force diagram for the crate and explain what the diagram tells you about the horizontal forces.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A 120 N sign hangs motionless from a vertical cable. Determine the force the cable exerts on the sign and explain why.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Two horizontal forces act on a cart: 35 N to the right and 20 N to the left. What is the net force on the cart?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A box slides to the right across a rough floor at constant velocity while a person pushes it to the right. Draw a force diagram for the box. Compare the sizes of the horizontal forces and justify your comparison.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A student says, “A rolling cart keeps moving because an inertia force pushes it forward.” Critique the statement using Newton’s First Law and the meaning of inertia.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Which situation is an example of dynamic equilibrium?
choices: A parked car with zero net force
A car moving in a straight line at constant velocity with zero net force
A car speeding up with a net force forward
A ball changing direction while moving at constant speed

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Three horizontal forces act on an object: 12 N east, 7 N west, and 3 N west. Determine the net force and describe the direction and relative length of the resultant-force arrow.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: During a cart trial, a student records, “The cart traveled 1.8 m in 3.0 s, so the wheels must have had very little friction.” Identify the observation and the inference. Explain the difference.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A book is resting on a horizontal table. Which pair of forces acts directly on the book?
choices: Weight downward and support force upward
Support force upward and motion force forward

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A phone rests on a seat inside a bus that is moving down the road. Describe the phone’s motion relative to the bus and relative to the road. Explain why both descriptions can be correct.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A lamp hangs motionless from the ceiling by one cord. Draw a force diagram for the lamp and explain how you know whether the forces are balanced.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A passenger is sitting in a moving train. Relative to which reference frame is the passenger at rest?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Two cyclists ride side by side at the same steady speed. Describe the motion of one cyclist relative to the other cyclist and relative to a person standing on the sidewalk.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: An elevator moves upward at constant velocity. What can you conclude about the net force on the elevator? Explain how the forces can be nonzero even though the net force is zero.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A mug stays fixed on a train table while a station platform moves backward in the window. Which statement is correct?
choices: The mug is at rest relative to the train and moving relative to the platform
The mug is moving relative to the train and at rest relative to the platform
The mug is at rest in every reference frame
The mug is moving at the same speed in every reference frame
The motion cannot be described without knowing the mug’s mass
